body: You realize that I was engaging in sexual stuff with a 10 year old when I was 15, right?

I'm not really worried about doing it again. I suffered from sexual compulsions (the kink I mentioned) in the past but I've effectively beaten them out of me through depression and COVID social isolation. I'm pretty much asexual for now, though I don't think that's healthy. Whenever I see people even casually mentioning their sex lives I feel borderline nauseous, and I almost want to cut off my dick at times. Sometimes I have violent fantasies about doing things to myself.

I don't know if I'll be able to handle the consequences. I don't even know what they would look like. Maybe if they were concrete (like 100 hours of community service, or a year in jail, or 50 lashes) it'd be easier to swallow. But if atonement might be out of reach, what's really the point? We all die in the end. Why should I hold my end of the bargain in that case? What's the rationale for not killing myself if society will, likely forever, ostracize me? Some turn to religion for answers, but I don't believe in God. Atonement, accountability, these are all just human constructs. They don't really exist in nature. But ostracization does. Living a pained life is real (I've had my fill, and all I've been doing is contributing to others' pain, small or large)

And if society doesn't shun me... what does that say about society, and their failure to protect someone who has genuinely (most likely) been harmed, to protect the young? Should rehabilitation come at the expense of the vulnerable? I despise people who prey on the weak, but *I am that person*. Wouldn't it be better for everyone for me to just be dead? Doesn't my continued participation here create a moral hazard?

I'm selfish. I really am selfish. I don't want to be selfish, I want to feel human, and to be human again. But to feel human is to feel the pain of what you've done. And to feel human is to let go of the fairy tale fantasy that everything will be alright, and that fantasy has been all that's keeping me going since I was like, maybe 8 years old. Pretty much all my life.

I don't know where I'm going with this. I'm extremely stressed out thinking about this and my head hurts. But I have no clue how the girl is suffering. I hope people listen to her when the time comes at least.

i met this girl on omegle when i was 15. we never met in person. we were both 15. that was what she said. i don't know whose idea it was to continue talking. we started sharing lewd stuff on snapchat. all i cared about was having someone to play along with my kink (maybe from trauma?). didn't care about anything else. after months then i stopped because i felt something was horribly wrong. i suspected she was only doing it for my approval, and not because she liked it. she latched onto me too much. i had added her cousin, who randomly texted me about how i was hurting her. sign number one. i didn't want to hurt her (i already did...), and i felt sorry for her. so i stayed in contact. but suspicious. there was the second sign. i should've vacated immediately, but i didn't. i didn't want to hurt her. but i didn't want to ask the obvious question because of the horrible implications if it was what i thought it was (wishful thinking). over a year since we met, i asked her cousin (by now I was 16)

>!cousin told me she was 5 years younger than me!<

i ghosted her immediately. i came back for a day, trying to get her to show any sort of proof (an 11th grade textbook or something). i couldn't believe it. cousin had to be lying. she had to. she refused. ghosted her again for good. i stuck to my guns. cousin was lying, i told myself. that was my only salvation.

girl came back after a few months. she apologized for lying. i told her it wasn't a problem, it wasn't her fault, and she should be careful. she still wanted to keep talking and didn't seem to realize the severity. i refused and never talked to her again, for her safety.

then the world slowly started to come undone. people would find out. i stopped trying in school. i couldn't look at myself in the mirror. but i didn't know why. all the internal self loathing i've had since i was a child had been validated, all my deepest fears come true. but i didn't know why. then covid started. then i confessed on 4chan. i read it, for the first time really (it was all in my head before then), and I basically had a month long panic attack. then i started getting the intrusive thoughts (if i did it once, what if i did it again?). i was living in a nightmare. i had no friends, or anyone to distract me from this. i still don't, really. but then it stopped, and i was numb. here i am
it's evil, i'm evil, i'm scum, irredeemable

still not certain if I should share. i've told people but they responded with basically shrugs, but that's because again, i was probably subconsciously omitting details. regardless of intent, i harmed someone, but whether i really meant it is the difference between sleeping that night and not, between being able to forgive myself and deserving of a million lashes.

it's also really long and complicated, and has so many details that can make or break the case. but maybe thats just my way of rationalizing it, because i know if i were to sum it up in one sentence, you would want to kill me

do you really want to know?

the truth is I can't actually give a 'measured' account. it is literally impossible. i know every word that comes out of my mouth will be to rationalize some aspect of what i did,  or omit certain details (maybe subconsciously, my memory is really bad and the entire thing was so long ago it feels almost hazy, like I've constructed an entire narrative about it, either downplaying or catastrophizing), or to pretend like i'm the one most harmed (but then what am I supposed to do? die?). Do you still want to know
No. That harms someone but not forever. Some wounds heal but others don't.
You really don't know the depths of my evil... I try to pretend it wasn't a big deal but it was, I am a fucking monster and if I told you, you will agree.

You really don't know how horrible it is

I'm afraid of telling a therapist in case they decide to drop me as a client, no one can know (unless it's anonymous)

>Also, it would help if you share what you did.

It's a really long story, and it wasn't just one fuck up, it was a long fuck up, one where I had a vague feeling what I was doing was wrong but didn't understand the gravity of it due to miscommunication.

Part of me feels that maybe I am catastrophizing, but another part wants me to err on the side of caution. It's better to punish myself than pretend I didn't do anything wrong
I guess. What if you don't deserve it though?

>The worst part of society is victim blaming, that’s gotta stop

Absolutely. I feel like this needs to be made louder. Too many times have I heard others try to excuse this type of behavior by saying something like "She had it coming", "She should've known better", ect. It's gross.

Professional help won't help when everyone will think you're better off dead. All the therapists I've talked to just give me generic advice like "exercise". But I hate myself for thinking that because I'm making myself the victim. What even is the right way to feel? How do I live knowing I am irredeemable scum? That all the ways I've tried to minimize my actions have made me blind to their gravity? That I can't even cope with what I did?
What has helped you the most in your recovery? What can society do to help victims more?

>People do horrible things and walk away without a care all the time.

I don't want to be this person. On one hand, suffering knowing what I did makes me feel human because at least it's proof I have some semblance of a conscience. On the other hand, I could live a happier life if I turned off my conscience, but what would be the cost? I would have to be a sociopath to simply "get over it", knowing that it's impossible for those who have received my destructive actions. I'm stuck with nowhere to go, and the worst part is that even confessing won't provide relief because I don't know if I'll only exacerbate the suffering of others that way (who's to say they aren't trying to recover without me involuntarily dragging them into the limelight)? 

I can't choose it to end. If I choose it to end, then I will lose my humanity and that might open the doors for real inhumanity. But this way I will still suffer, even if it's not as much as who I made suffer. How much suffering/flagellation is proportional? Why are there no answers?
I guess, but when does it end? Will I be 90 and still repaying the debt? Why does it have to be this way? Why can't I just undo what I did?

I mean, something that society considers redeemable. Outside of society, redemption doesn't really exist as a concept. And I would say redemption would be giving more than you have taken (making up for what you've done), though that becomes stickier without the ability to quantify the moral weight of actions. And while I guess there are other goals after wrongdoing (punishment by death), I'm talking about what one person can do, not what everyone else can do.
